helpIntro: Illinois Tech uses a 4.0 undergraduate GPA scale: A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, E/NA=0. Enter graded semester credit hours and final grades to estimate your cumulative or projected GPA.
helpNote: For Mies-campus undergraduate cumulative GPA. P/F, S/U, transfer, audit, withdrawal and temporary grades are excluded. Major GPA is a separate subset. Graduate and Chicago-Kent Law records use separate rules. Repeat Impact is only an estimate for an approved undergraduate grade-exclusion repeat.
helpExample: A 3-credit A earns 12 quality points and a 3-credit B earns 9; 21 ÷ 6 = 3.500.

gradeExplanations.A: A = 4.00 quality points per graded credit hour.
gradeExplanations.B: B = 3.00 quality points per graded credit hour.
gradeExplanations.C: C = 2.00 quality points per graded credit hour.
gradeExplanations.D: D = 1.00 quality point per graded credit hour for undergraduate work.
gradeExplanations.E: E = 0.00; its graded credit hours still count in GPA.
gradeExplanations.NA: NA is equivalent to E for GPA calculations and counts at 0.00.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete is excluded until a final grade is posted.
gradeExplanations.R: Research (R) is temporary and excluded from GPA until resolved.
gradeExplanations.F: F on the P/F basis is excluded from the institutional GPA.
gradeExplanations.TR: Transfer credit is excluded from Illinois Tech cumulative and major GPA.
gradeExplanations.X: X is temporary and excluded until a final grade is posted.

specialTypes.name: Illinois Tech undergraduate course
specialTypes.note: Use for Mies-campus undergraduate A/B/C/D/E/NA grades and excluded notations.

specialTypes.name: Transfer credit / external course
specialTypes.note: Accepted transfer credit may apply to the degree, but transfer grades are excluded from Illinois Tech cumulative and major GPA.

specialTypes.name: Chicago-Kent College of Law course
specialTypes.note: Chicago-Kent has its own grading scale and calculators; do not use the Mies-campus undergraduate mapping.

repeatPolicy.note: Use Repeat Impact only for an approved undergraduate grade-exclusion repeat of the same course with the same credits and an eligible final second grade. The second grade replaces the first in GPA even if lower.
